item.title: Things to Do, DMV: Weekend Rundown, March 5-8
item.description: From biblical epics to financial workshops, paint and sip nights to urban agriculture events, and a St. Patrick's Day parade to an International Women's Day celebration, there are a variety of events happening in the DMV this weekend! The post Things to Do, DMV: Weekend Rundown, March 5-8 appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: From Lament to Action: Baltimore Church Backs Racial Repair
item.description: The Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.) has launched the Reparative Justice Initiative, an ambitious plan to dismantle deep-seated bias and poverty in Baltimore, which includes allocating 15% of year-end non-committed funds to support Black churches and communities. The post From Lament to Action: Baltimore Church Backs Racial Repair appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: DCPSC Awards $3M Contract for Solar Pilot Project in D.C.
item.description: The DCPSC has awarded a $3 million contract to Ecogy Energy and Ecosuite to develop a solar aggregation pilot project that will use advanced inverter technology to improve the reliability of the District's electric grid and reduce strain during times of high demand. The post DCPSC Awards $3M Contract for Solar Pilot Project in D.C. appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Henrietta Lacks Family Secures Settlement With Novartis Over HeLa Cells
item.description: The Lacks family has reached a confidential settlement with Novartis, resolving a lawsuit that accused the company of profiting from the use of Henrietta Lacks' cells without her knowledge. The post Henrietta Lacks Family Secures Settlement With Novartis Over HeLa Cells appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: D.C. Gas Prices Poised to Climb After Iran Strikes Shake Oil Markets
item.description: Gas prices in the D.C. area are currently about $3.10 per gallon, but are expected to rise due to U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran, which sent global oil prices higher and increased volatility in energy markets. The post D.C. Gas Prices Poised to Climb After Iran Strikes Shake Oil Markets appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: District of Columbia Among Nation’s Top Places for Women, New Report Shows
item.description: The District of Columbia ranked second in the nation for women's economic and social well-being, health care, and safety, according to a new WalletHub report, with Massachusetts ranking first overall. The post District of Columbia Among Nation’s Top Places for Women, New Report Shows appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Remembering the Legacy of Rev. Jesse L. Jackson: ‘You Hold On, and Hold Out’
item.description: Rev. Jesse Jackson's legacy of service to the country and the world is being celebrated across the nation, as he lies in honor at the South Carolina State House before continuing to Washington, D.C., and then to his beloved Chicago, with his family being thanked for sharing their husband and father. The post Remembering the Legacy of Rev. Jesse L. Jackson: ‘You Hold On, and Hold Out’ appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: ASALH Celebrates ‘A Century of Black History Commemorations’ During Annual Luncheon
item.description: The Association for the Study of African American Life and History (ASALH) held its annual Black History Month Luncheon to celebrate the achievements of the Black community and to call for continued advocacy and empowerment, with a focus on building a foundation of truth and education for the next generation. The post ASALH Celebrates ‘A Century of Black History Commemorations’ During Annual Luncheon appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Black and Latino Workers Face Lower Pay, Higher Joblessness in DC Fiscal Policy Institute Report
item.description: Despite Washington, D.C.'s prosperous skyline, Black and Latino workers face significant economic disparities, with lower wages, higher unemployment, and unaffordable housing costs, due to decades of racial inequality. The post Black and Latino Workers Face Lower Pay, Higher Joblessness in DC Fiscal Policy Institute Report appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: When $250 Keeps You in Jail: The Personal Story Behind a National Bail Showdown
item.description: The Bail Project is a nonprofit organization that provides free bail assistance to those in need and advocates for better policies in the pretrial justice system, having supported over 40,000 people since its founding.
